title: Normalized finite-fibre root-descent data
statement: For the finite tame category $\mathcal C_Q$, root tower $X$ and inertia group $G$ of [def-sfb-snc-finite-tame-sheaves], define normalized finite-fibre classification data as follows. Use the actual profinite test functor $X[P]$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] and its constant-label sections [def-sfb-profinite-product-maps]. A root deck map $X[G]\to X$ lies over $U^\circ$, gives the torsor comparison $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ as an isomorphism, and rotates every prime-power root by the chosen primitive root raised to the corresponding adic residue; it fixes coefficients. A classification consists of this deck map, a fully faithful functor $\mathcal C_Q\to\mathrm{ContAction}(\mathrm{Fintype},G)$ [def-pod-finite-continuous-module], an identification of its underlying set functor with the actual geometric stalk, and for every object a universal section on $X[Q_F]$ whose restrictions give bijections on every object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its label germs are the given stalk identification. These sections are natural in every sheaf morphism. The category has finite products, preserved by its inclusion and fibre functor. On the whole scheme $X[G\times Q_F]$, restricting the universal section by $(x,g,q)\mapsto(x,gq)$ equals restricting it by $(x,g,q)\mapsto(gx,q)$, the latter map pinned by both product projections. For an internal finite-ring module [def-pod-internal-module], define a linear fibre to be a finite continuous linear representation with an equivariant identification of its carrier with this fibre; addition, zero, negation and scalar maps on all generalized elements agree under that identification. The residual chart, refinement and root-coordinate data are those of [def-sfb-snc-residual-chart-data]. For a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose underlying set sheaf belongs to $\mathcal C_Q$, its normalized label in the actual module stalk is the germ of its universal section at that label. A module stalk action is a homomorphism from $G$ to the linear endomorphisms of that stalk sending every normalized label to the label transformed by the classifier action; hence it is pinned by all labels.
